title: A minor's chat and wellbeing data leaks through a contractor export
setting: Murshid serves Dubai private-school students aged 13-17 under school licences and family plans. All names and numbers below are synthetic.

events.text: Monitoring alert: a debugging export of chat logs (412 student records, Grades 9-11, ages 14-17: names, class, planner entries and wellbeing check-in notes) was written to a publicly readable storage bucket by a contractor's script on Sunday night. Access logs show three downloads from unknown IP addresses.
A parent emails the school counsellor: her son's Murshid wellbeing note about exam stress has been posted in a student WhatsApp group. The school did not know Murshid stored wellbeing notes.
A guardian files a complaint with the UAE Data Office saying an AI study app leaked her daughter's personal data and nobody has told her what happened.
Forensics update: the bucket belongs to the model-logging vendor and is hosted outside the UAE. 37 of the 412 records came in through a school-connector licence; the rest are family accounts.
A news site runs the story 'AI tutor leaks teenagers' mental-health notes'. The Child Digital Safety Council secretariat and the Ministry of Education are asked for comment.
